 Saudi Pro League agrees big match broadcast deal with Footballco’s GOAL platform
 23rd October 2026 
 By Paul Nicholson 
-->
 October 23 – The Saudi Pro League (SPL) has partnered with Footballco to show high-profile matches through GOAL’s Front Three, its creator-led YouTube and social video brand, combining live coverage with watch-a-longs.
 The broadcasts will run in the UK and Ireland, Belgium, the Nordic countries and Canada.
 They start on October 23 with Al-Qadsiah against Al-Hilal, a top-of-the-table game featuring Brendan Rodgers in the Qadsiah dugout and former Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders against an Al-Hilal side including Ollie Watkins and Gabriel Martinelli. The Jeddah Derby between Al-Ittihad and Al-Ahli follows on November 26, then Al-Nassr against Al-Hilal on December 10.
 Footballco’s Middle East brand Yalla GOAL will handle build-up, with clips shared afterwards across TikTok, Facebook, YouTube and Instagram.
 The deal is part of the league’s new distribution model, launched in September with Recast, which lets approved publishers stream live matches on their own platforms in 16 markets. Footballco will also stream matches on GOAL through Recast.
 “We’ve seen this approach work before, with our watch-a-long broadcast and social content from last year’s Riyadh Derby being viewed 3.8 million times,” said Andy Jackson, Footballco’s SVP for the Middle East. “We also recognize that we have an opportunity to grow awareness and fandom of the RSL in these markets, through GOAL’s Front Three broadcasts, which can then translate into a transactional relationship on our website.”
 Mohamed Rassmy, the league’s digital media rights director, said: “By combining live football with the reach and influence of established digital creators, we can engage fans on the platforms they already use, while making the RSL more accessible and building stronger relationships with supporters around the world.”
 The league says the deal complements its existing coverage across more than 180 territories with 45 partners. IMG holds worldwide media distribution rights through 2028-29.
